steps.title: Protect the passer
steps.body: A quarterback in his throwing motion has his ==eyes downfield== and can't brace for contact. The rule keeps the most ==defenseless player== on the field from taking needless hits.

steps.title: No late, high or low hits
steps.body: Once the ==ball is out==, a rusher gets about one step to pull up. He also can't hit the passer in the ==head or neck==, or at the ==knees or below==.

steps.title: Too late
steps.body: A rusher gets about ==one step== after the ball leaves. Here he takes two more and drives through the passer. That's roughing.

steps.title: Head and knees
steps.body: Even an on-time hit is a foul if it lands on the ==head or neck== or goes ==low at the knees==. The strike zone is chest to thighs.

steps.title: The body slam
steps.body: A rusher can't ==land on the passer with his full body weight==. The legal move is to wrap him up and ==roll off== to the side.

steps.title: Fifteen yards
steps.body: Roughing the passer is a ==15-yard== penalty plus an ==automatic first down==. It's one of the costliest flags a defense can draw.
steps.note: Ref signal: the personal-foul signal, then a throwing motion.

options: The rusher hit the quarterback low
The hit came after the ball was gone
The quarterback was out of the pocket
steps.explain: The ball was already out when the rusher arrived. He had time to pull up and drove through the passer anyway: 15 yards and an automatic first down.

steps.prompt: Which hit on the passer is legal?
options: Hitting his helmet as he throws
Wrapping him at the waist as he releases
Landing on him with full body weight
steps.explain: An on-time hit in the strike zone, chest to thighs, is legal. High hits, low hits and body slams are all roughing.
